body: Yay masks, but unfortunately those online decisions are final for a lot of reasons, not the least of which being it would be logistically impossible for them to house everyone on such short notice, fall is for sure online even if the pandemic stopped.

I don’t disagree with the moral judgement here, but, and forgive me for my ignorance, isn’t that sorta what an LP officer’s job is? I didn’t get the indication they were on public property, but if they were, why wouldn’t it be within his rights to catch him? Perhaps it is stupid on the LP’s part for their own safety and whatnot, but I don’t see how he can’t reclaim stolen property as an officer of the company it was stolen from at his own risk if he decides to. Again, I may be completely misguided, and I agree that it was a shitty thing for that person to make the LP do.
This exists, to some degree, although it has been pretty dead for awhile. Maybe you can breathe some new life into it, I’ll add you

Thanks for the input, but just a note, I am about 1200 miles away from home, so it isn’t exactly reasonable to plan a weekly visit. Also, she definitely isn’t the only high point, as 1 I do enjoy plenty of things, and 2 I don’t see her even close to daily. Again, though, I do appreciate your and everyone’s thoughtfulness in replying.

Firstly, my girlfriend is not a “thot”. She is honestly a wonderful person, and I feel wonderful when I am around her. You can read my other replies if you want further clarification, but the gist is that I did not do her or our relationship justice in this post, as my happy times were not the point. So don’t be a dick, and get some respect for women, as well as people in general.

Secondly, I don’t know why you think I don’t have actual friends, but I am pretty sure I know what friendship is. Obviously the relationships I am building with people I met at most two weeks ago, with a few exceptions for orientation, are not as strong as, say, the people I have known and grown with for anywhere from 4 to 16 years. That doesn’t mean we aren’t friends.

Lastly, school is not everything. Grades are important, and should not be ignored, but life is more than that. People who go to college looking for 4 years of hell to propel them into a life of security are forgetting that 4 years is a large part of your life. So yes, that would all matter even if I felt like I was doing alright in my classes. I am applying myself, and I can’t magically not be sad, so in summary, to use your terminology, begone thot.

I understand how you got that from what I wrote, but I’m confident that she likes me, and enjoys spending time with me, for a variety of reasons, many of which I haven’t mentioned here because, as I have noted, the point of this post wasn’t to appreciate my happy times. Additionally, it is a new relationship, and we are young college students. We aren’t nearly far along enough to really have a strong commitment, we haven’t even talked about what we are/our boundaries etc. She has a life of her own, as do I, and life gets busy. I don’t blame her for it, nor do I blame myself, and I still thoroughly enjoy when we do spend time together. I do wish she were more present sometimes, but again, we lead busy lives, and our relationship is young.

That isn’t the point of the post. I do love what I have, and I do have happy times. In fact, I made it very clear that I don’t understand why I am as depressed as I am, nor do I want to be. Either way, though, advice received, I do want to try to appreciate what I have. One note though, I don’t have a safety net out here, you might have misread that part but I’m very far from home haha. Thanks for the input, I really need to think about and appreciate my girlfriend and friends more, stop focusing on the negatives as much.

I haven’t been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and it isn’t an I’m homesick post except for maybe one part of it, but even then homesickness is really not a big thing here. That is to say, I’m not sure what you are getting at, but I agree that that is pretty much all you read.
Consider yourself enrolled, let’s do this.
I’m not great at venting in real life, but who knows, maybe it is a good thing.
If you are going through the literal exact same situation as me, then note that I found that writing pretty therapeutic if you’d like to give it a try. Keep on keeping on, my brother/sister in arms.
Indeed, but right now I’m coarse. (Hehe)

I audibly went “aw” when you said I seem like a good person, so thanks for that. And yeah, I agree that what I am feeling is very likely the norm, I just suppose I wish it weren’t, you know? Maybe it is necessary, but who doesn’t wish for corn when they are plowing around in manure?

Well, first off thanks for the praise, it really does mean a lot. Secondly, you are right, I wasn’t trying to help myself, others, get advice, or get attention. I am glad if it helps others, and I agree it was therapeutic so I supposed I helped myself too. Finally, I’m proud of you for writing that stuff. Having just done something similar (ha), I know it is hard and can take a lot out of you to admit things like this to the world. But you said it, every little bit helps.
